questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column
questions.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & \sqrt{2} & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & \sqrt{3} & 1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{13}+\sqrt{2}\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+\sqrt{3}\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot (-1)^{2+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|+\sqrt{3}\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|-\sqrt{3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the third row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+2\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(1\cdot 1-2\cdot (-1)) \\  & =2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|=-2\cdot 6=-12.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $4$th row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot {C}_{41}+0\cdot {C}_{42}+0\cdot {C}_{43}+1\cdot {C}_{44} \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{4+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{21}+0\cdot {C}_{22}+0\cdot {C}_{23} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2(16-(-2)) \\  & =-36\end{aligned}
$$

 
Finally, we compute the second $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along its $3$rd row:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+1\cdot {C}_{32}+(-2)\cdot {C}_{33} \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-2)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(0-4)-2(2-2) \\  & =4+0 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|=-3\cdot (-36)+1\cdot 4=112.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Row
questions.problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the third row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+2\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| & =4\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(3\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot (-2)) \\  & =4\cdot 4 \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|=-2\cdot 16=-32.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant Using a Laplace Expansion Across a Column
questions.worked_solution:
Using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| & =(-2)\cdot {C}_{13}+0\cdot {C}_{23}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+1\cdot {C}_{43} \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot (-1)^{4+3}\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}|-|\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 5 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
